messages:
anya: quick follow-up on the attention memory layout RFC — I hacked a small prototype showing effects of NHWC vs NCHW + contiguous vs interleaved QKV on kernel selection. numbers below and a proposal for a minimal runtime ABI change.
marc: can you paste the numbers?
anya: local perf (A100, seq=512, heads=32, d_head=64)
anya: - NHWC + interleaved QKV: 1.0ms/token (baseline)
anya: - NCHW + contiguous QKV: 0.78ms/token (-22%)
anya: - NHWC + contiguous QKV: 0.85ms/token (-15%)
anya: - NCHW + interleaved QKV: 0.95ms/token (-5%)
liz: interesting. did you control for memory bandwidth vs kernel launch overhead?
anya: yes — used persistent kernels where possible; differences remain mostly in GEMM shapes and memcpy patterns. cache hit rates for KV cache also shifted: contiguous QKV makes prefix caching simpler (single buffer copy) which improves streaming.
sam: what about attention kernels that expect interleaved QKV (qkv interleaved layout optimizations)? we have a lot of optimized paths for that, right?
anya: right — we still have those kernels. the point is the runtime should pick the best kernel given the shape/layout metadata instead of assuming layout. currently the selector uses model.arch + dtype + seq_len heuristics; we need to include layout fields.
ops-bot: deploy-check: runtime-selector change flagged (config env RUNTIME_SELECTOR_LAYOUT=true)
tzu-chen: +1 to including layout. but this affects saved checkpoints/serialized weights for Dedicated/Private customers. if we standardize on contiguous QKV for runtime-only, we need deterministic transformation tooling at load time.
anya: proposal: add a small `layout_hint` to ServeRequest metadata and ModelManifest.
anya: ```
layout_hint:
  tensor_format: "NHWC" | "NCHW"
  qkv_order: "interleaved" | "contiguous"
  stride_info: "bytes_per_element" # optional
```
anya: runtime selector uses layout_hint first; if absent, falls back to legacy heuristics and may trigger a one-time reformat stage (fast transpose/pack).
marc: what about API surface with private deploys? manifest change is fine but need backward compat. also we should provide a `repack_on_load` flag to avoid long startup times for huge models.
liz: also watch out for quantized kernels: int8 kernels often assume a specific packing. transformation must also produce quantized-friendly layout or we risk losing perf.
sam: another thought — storage vs memory contract. keep checkpoint format neutral (tensor dims + strides) and let runtime pack into device memory representation. this keeps on-disk stable and gives runtime freedom.
tzu-chen: agreed. add `device_packed_layout` in runtime config to choose packing at deploy time. for Dedicated we can choose NCHW+contiguous if it's fastest for that fleet.
anya: good. implications for KV cache APIs: we should expose KV cache as an opaque buffer with a well-defined shape descriptor that includes the same layout fields. avoids per-kernel assumptions.
anya: example KV descriptor: `kv = { format: "NCHW", layout: "contiguous", head_dim: 64, heads: 32, seq_len: 512, dtype: "fp16" }`
marc: can we avoid adding too many enums? lean set: tensor_format + qkv_order + dtype should be sufficient. stride_info optional.
liz: ops that mutate buffer (rotary, bias add, reorder) need to be in the runtime op library so we can pipeline repacks. otherwise customers end up shipping custom transforms.
sam: perf regression testing note: add a per-model microbenchmark that exercises packing transition (cold load, after repack) and streaming steady state. We'll add checks to Optimize.
anya: open questions: 1) default on-disk format? 2) should runtime ever rewrite checkpoints on disk (dangerous for Private) or only create device-side caches? 3) how to version the layout_hint in manifests for compatibility?
marc: my votes: 1) neutral on-disk (tensor dims + strides), 2) never rewrite on-disk for Private (only device-side caches), 3) use semvered manifest field (layout_hint.v1) and allow fallback.
tzu-chen: we'll need a migration guide for partners and a CLI `redwood pack-model --target device_layout` utility.
ops-bot: task-created: #infra-1234 add layout_hint to ModelManifest, update selector, add microbench harness
anya: I'll write a short RFC follow-up with prototype code and a test plan. tagging people who volunteered: @marc @liz @tzu-chen @sam. any objections to making layout a first-class selection key?
marc: none here. +1 :thumbsup:
liz: +1, but add quantized kernel tests before rollout.
sam: +1. please include streaming KV cache scenarios in the matrics.
tzu-chen: +1, will coordinate on packaging CLI.
anya: thanks — I'll post the draft RFC in #eng-runtime tomorrow. if anyone wants to poke at prototype code sooner I pushed branch `layout-select-proto` to repo (link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/tree/layout-select-proto).
marc: will review later today.
liz: quick nit — let's call the field `memory_layout_hint` to be explicit.
anya: good call. I'll use that name.
ops-bot: reminder: deploy-check passed for branch layout-select-proto on CI (all green)
anya: thanks all, closing this thread for now.
